title: WCET Builds the Case for Its Combined Value
summary: WCET asked Ricochet to redesign its brand architecture so both of its member groups can see why a combined membership is worth keeping.

sections.heading: What was holding WCET back?
sections.body: WCET, the technology-focused membership program of the Western Interstate Commission for Higher Education, serves more than 365 member institutions. Its members fall into two distinct groups of higher education professionals whose needs don't always overlap. As college and university budgets tighten, every membership faces closer review. WCET needed a clear way to show both audiences why the combined membership is worth keeping, and its brand was not making that case on its own.

sections.heading: What did Ricochet build?
sections.body: Ricochet is leading a full brand architecture redesign that reaches into member benefits and product consolidation. The work draws on WCET's current messaging, collateral, member journey and competitive landscape. Ricochet is reviewing WCET's brand standards against its January 2026 visual refresh to set new visual design standards. The team is also documenting the member benefits available at each membership tier. Every piece is planned with future AI-assisted marketing collateral in mind.

sections.heading: What changed for WCET's members?
sections.body: The work is still in progress, so results are not in yet. The goal is a clear, tested way for WCET to explain the value of belonging to both sides of its membership. When the redesign is complete, members in each group should be able to see which benefits come with their tier and why the combined membership serves them. That message will rest on research rather than assumption.

title: ARA Drives a Digital Transformation

sections.heading: What was holding ARA back?
sections.body: The American Retirement Association (ARA) serves more than 30,000 members, but it had no Chief Technology Officer and no technology leadership of any kind. Its systems were outdated and were limiting business performance. ARA's website also badly needed an update. With no one in place to set technology priorities or guide the work, ARA turned to Ricochet.

sections.heading: What did Ricochet do?
sections.body: Ricochet Chief Consultant Chris Gloede stepped in as temporary CTO. He set project priorities and evaluated the tech team's skills, giving ARA the strategic guidance it lacked. Ricochet also took charge of the website update and the search for a new platform. It wrote the Request for Proposal and managed the process from agency invitations and presentations through proposal evaluation, then coordinated selection of the best agency.

sections.heading: What changed for ARA's members?

A new website on a new platform, built by a carefully chosen agency, will give members a better digital front door to the association. With clear technology priorities in place, ARA is better equipped to serve members as their digital expectations keep changing.

title: BSCAI Boosts Sales with HubSpot
summary: BSCAI's prospect data was scattered across systems and spreadsheets until Ricochet set up HubSpot Sales Hub with an eight-stage pipeline for corporate membership sales.

sections.heading: What was holding BSCAI back?
sections.body: The Building Service Contractors Association International (BSCAI) has more than 1,000 member companies from the United States and 15 countries worldwide. sections.heading: What did Ricochet build?
sections.body: Ricochet first helped BSCAI acquire HubSpot Sales Hub, handling the requirements and fee negotiations. Working with staff, it designed a structured sales pipeline with eight stages and wrote new sales collateral and phone scripts for each one. Ricochet automated key tasks to free staff from repetitive manual work like data entry. It also built pipeline reporting so management can track progress and spot bottlenecks.

sections.heading: What changed for BSCAI's members?

Every prospect moves through a clear eight-stage pipeline, and the sales team has the right materials and scripts ready at each step. With less time lost to data entry, staff can spend more of their day talking with prospective members. Management can see where deals stall and act sooner.
